content.content: Annie Easley was born and raised in Birmingham, Alabama. In 1955 she began work at the Aircraft Engine Research Laboratory in Cleveland, Ohio, which later became NASA’s Glenn Research Center. She started as a “human computer,” doing difficult calculations by hand, and when electronic computers arrived she became a computer programmer. She wrote and tested code used to study energy-conversion systems and for the Centaur upper-stage rocket, and her code also helped analyze the battery technology used in early hybrid vehicles. She also served as an equal employment opportunity counselor, helping supervisors deal with complaints about gender, race and age. Her career lasted 34 years, and she died on June 25, 2011. (Practice passage written for this packet from NASA’s biography of Annie Easley, nasa.gov.)
Multiple-choice rule: tap ONE letter only. If you change your mind, tap the one you want instead.
